name: repeat-matching
title: Repeat- and reproducibility-matching vs the BioSimulators reference study
claim: On the BIOMD1-3 validation subset, the live engines reproduce the BioSimulators SED-ML reference arm exactly wherever an observable is computed: after iteration 2 ("full observable coverage"), all 12 repeat arms (copasi/tellurium/amici/pysces × the models they cover) match the reference under numpy allclose with zero numerical mismatches; the only residual is coverage (2 reference observables in BIOMD3 are not yet computed by any engine). Cross-engine reproducibility is likewise exact where observables overlap (22/30 pairs exact; the 8 residuals are pysces computing 2/65 observables differently and simbio exposing a reduced 48-observable set). The dominant failure mode is observable coverage, not numerical divergence — confirming the study hypothesis.
question: Do the current cross-simulator BioModels runs reproduce the BioSimulators SED-ML reference results engine-for-engine (repeat matching), and where they diverge, can any previous cross-engine open questions be closed (reproducibility matching)?
hypothesis: Where an observable is computed at all, the current study reproduces the previous study exactly; the dominant failure mode is coverage (missing SED-ML dataGenerator observables) rather than numerical divergence. Each recovered reproducibility match — especially bringing simbio, the new engine, onto the engines that already agree — is worth 10x a broken repeat match.
objective: Run the BioModels validation subset under the live engines (COPASI, Tellurium, simbio, AMICI, PySCeS) plus the BioSimulators SED-ML reference arm, score repeat-match (live X vs reference X) and reproducibility-match (cross-engine) with numpy allclose, iterate the observable-coverage fixes, and report every remaining mismatch with analysis.
description: The batch-compare-biomodels composite fetches each model's SBML, parses every SED-ML dataGenerator, runs each live engine, and scores two match kinds against the committed BioSimulators reference: repeat (live engine X vs reference X, same engine) and reproducibility (cross-engine, live A vs live B). Iteration 1 computed a partial observable set (17/48 reference observables missing on BIOMD1-2); iteration 2 extended the dataGenerator handling to full observable coverage. Results committed at studies/repeat-matching/results/ iter{1,2}_subset_match_summary.parquet.
readouts: repeat_arms_matched_exact — repeat arms where matched == total (numerical agreement)
repeat_arms_full_coverage — repeat arms where missing == 0 (all reference observables computed)
reproducibility_pairs_exact — cross-engine pairs where matched == total
residual_coverage_gap — reference observables in BIOMD3 not computed by any engine (=2)

findings.statement: After the iteration-2 coverage fix, every repeat arm reproduces the BioSimulators reference exactly: 12/12 arms have matched == total under numpy allclose, with zero numerical mismatches.
findings.next_action: Scale the repeat-match harness to the full corpus against the complete BioSimulators reference set.

findings.statement: The residual failures are coverage, not numerics: iteration 1 left 17/48 reference observables uncomputed on BIOMD1-2; iteration 2 closed that to 0 there and 2 on BIOMD3 (SED-ML dataGenerator forms not yet supported). This confirms the hypothesis that the dominant failure mode is missing observables rather than divergent trajectories.
findings.next_action: Implement the remaining SED-ML dataGenerator shapes to close the BIOMD3 2-observable gap.

findings.statement: Cross-engine reproducibility is exact where observables overlap: 22/30 iter2 pairs match fully. The 8 residuals are understood — pysces computes 2/65 observables differently from copasi/tellurium/amici on BIOMD1, and simbio exposes a reduced 48-observable set (those 48 all agree). simbio, the new engine, lands on the engines that already agree.
findings.next_action: Investigate the 2 pysces observables on BIOMD1 and simbio's reduced observable export.

regression_compatibility.basis: Both iterations completed without error; the iter2 run is committed and re-scoreable from the parquet.

biological_validation.basis: On the 3-model validation subset the repeat-match gate passes: all computed observables reproduce the BioSimulators reference exactly. Scope is the subset, not the full corpus.

explanatory_gain.basis: F-02 identifies the mechanism — residual mismatch is observable coverage (unsupported SED-ML dataGenerators), not numerical divergence — which redirects effort from "chase trajectory differences" to "finish dataGenerator support".

conclusion_logic.if_primary_tests_pass: The live engines reproduce the BioSimulators reference exactly on the BIOMD1-3 subset wherever an observable is computed; residuals are coverage, not numerics. Proceed to scale the repeat-match harness to the full corpus and close the remaining dataGenerator coverage gaps.
conclusion_logic.if_primary_tests_fail: A repeat arm disagreeing numerically with its reference on a commonly computed observable would mean a real engine/encoding divergence; root-cause the specific (engine, model, observable) before scaling the harness.

limitations:
Scope is the BIOMD1-3 validation subset, not the full BioModels corpus. The corpus-scale BioSimulators reference set (datasets/biosimulators_sedml_results, ~2.6 GB) is gitignored and the corpus-scale repeat-match run is not yet done.
2 reference observables in BIOMD3 remain uncomputed by every engine (unsupported SED-ML dataGenerator forms) — a coverage gap, not a mismatch.
Single seed (seed 0); these are deterministic ODE integrations, so a seed sweep is not the relevant robustness axis (observable/model coverage is).
falsifiability: A repeat arm whose live engine disagrees numerically with its own BioSimulators reference on an observable both compute (matched < total with missing == 0) would falsify the "coverage, not numerics" claim. No such arm exists in iteration 2.
